title: The IFCASL Corpus of French and German Non-native and Native Read Speech
domain: French/German; L2 phonetics; native/non-native read speech; pronunciation; segmental/prosodic production
manual_annotation_evidence: The corpus paper reports about 100 speakers with comparable productions, word- and phone-level segmentation/annotation, and more than 50% manually corrected data; project documentation says automatic speech-text alignment was followed by manual checking/annotation for both French and German native and non-native speech.
lineage_issue: Primary recordings were created by the IFCASL project, so there is no secondary-recording lineage problem apparent. The unresolved issue is isolating exactly which files/tiers are manually corrected versus alignment-only before promotion.
public_access: Publication and project documentation are public; a stable public corpus-data deposit/download was not identified in this pass.
license_or_terms: Publication is CC BY 4.0 via ACL Anthology; corpus-data license/redistribution terms still need verification.
next_action: Locate the corpus distribution or institutional deposit; enumerate audio/annotation files; identify the manually corrected subset/tier provenance and ingest only verified manual/corrected word/phone annotations plus all supplied production measurements and metadata.
notes: Especially valuable for second-language phonetics because it includes French learners of German, German learners of French, and native comparison subcorpora. Keep in HIGH review until public data location and exact tier-level provenance are verified.
